notes: Mandatory for all Registered Members. First responsibility is community welfare, health, and safety. 8+ clauses covering professional reputation, legal compliance (including SEC regulations), and ethical conduct. Separate Code of Conduct for events/community.

organization: Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct Regulations
notes: All AusIMM members must comply. Professional Standards Compliance Process (PSCP) enforces accountability. Includes separate Code for Consultants. JORC (mineral resources reporting) and VALMIN (valuation) codes set technical standards. Peak body and trusted voice for Australian resources sector.

organization: Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining
notes: Approved by Trustees per Royal Charter. Members must behave honourably, be truthful/honest with clients/colleagues. Public good overrides client obligations. Includes Whistleblowing Guide and Equity/Diversity/Inclusion guidance. Regulates Chartered professionals (CEng, CGeol, CSci, etc.).

document_title: Code of Professional Conduct for Members
notes: Preamble + Fundamental Principle + 12 Canons. Covers competency, honesty, ethics, conflicts of interest, public health and safety, environmental impact, anti-bribery/corruption, observance of law. Revised 2014. One of the most comprehensive petroleum engineering ethics documents.

October 2013 version. AAPG has 38,000+ members in 100+ countries. Members shall not use AAPG membership to imply endorsement of specific projects. Violation subject to disciplinary action per Bylaws. Covers geological practice in relation to petroleum, natural gas, and subsurface fluids.

Three-tier structure: Canons (broad principles), Ethical Standards (aspirational goals), Rules of Conduct (mandatory). Compliance with Rules of Conduct mandatory; violation grounds for disciplinary action up to membership termination. Covers personal integrity, public welfare, honesty in communication.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
notes: Approved by GSA Council September 2019 — first enforceable ethics code in GSA history. Includes mandatory standards and aspirational standards. Covers research misconduct, discrimination, harassment, bullying. 15 formal complaints received since 2019; 6 resulting in sanctions. Also applies to award recipients.

Applies to all Fellows irrespective of grade or whether acting professionally or personally. Incorporates American Geosciences Institute Guidelines and Science Council Guidelines for Chartered Scientists. Council may remove Fellow for serious breach. Covers professional practice integrity, public interest, and safe/welcoming events environment.

document_title: Scientific Integrity and Professional Ethics Policy
notes: Adopted 2017; updated 2023. Based on Singapore Statement on Research Integrity (2010). Identifies harassment, discrimination, and bullying as scientific misconduct. Applies to all AGU members, staff, volunteers, and non-members in AGU activities. Sanctions mechanisms in place. Relevant to geological/geophysical work in mining and petroleum.

organization: Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum
document_title: Code of Conduct / Professional Standards for Qualified Persons
notes: Members must observe standards of business and personal ethics; demonstrate honesty and integrity; comply with applicable laws and policies. Whistleblower policy; no retaliation protections. Qualified Person (QP) professional standing provides legal accountability for public mineral disclosures. CIM standards incorporated into NI 43-101 (Canadian securities law).

organization: International Council on Mining and Metals
profession_name: Mining and metals industry executive / company
notes: Founded 2001; 10 Principles published 2003; updated periodically. Principles: Ethical Business, Decision Making, Human Rights, Risk Management, Health & Safety, Environmental Performance, Conservation of Biodiversity, Responsible Production, Social Performance, Stakeholder Engagement. Mandatory for all 27 company members (represent ~1/3 of global mining/metals). Annual assurance reporting required. CEO-led organization.

document_title: Towards Sustainable Mining (TSM) — Guiding Principles and 8 Protocols
notes: Established 2004. First mining standard requiring site-level reporting with external verification. 8 protocols, 30 sustainability performance indicators. Annual self-assessment mandatory for MAC members (Canadian operations); external verification every 3 years. Multi-stakeholder Community of Interest (COI) Panel oversees development. Adopted by mining associations in 13+ countries.

Every WCA member is signatory to the RCP. Principles cover social/economic responsibility, integrity, climate change/emissions mitigation, environmental protection, biodiversity. WCA rebranded to FutureCoal in November 2023 with new Sustainable Coal Stewardship (SCS) framework.

document_title: API Auditor Code of Ethics and Conduct
profession_name: Petroleum industry professional / API certification participant
notes: Applies to all API certification program participants (applicants and licensed/certified organizations and their employees). Covers: legal compliance, conflict of interest disclosure, confidentiality, anti-harassment. Non-compliance may result in withdrawal of application or license/certificate termination.

Principles agreed 2003 (Lancaster House Conference). EITI Standard 2019 replaced EITI Rules (2011). 57 member countries. Requires disclosure of licenses, contracts, beneficial ownership, production volumes, payments, revenue allocation. Anti-corruption and accountability as core ethics content. Not a professional code but a governance ethics standard.

document_title: Responsible Mining Standard (Workers' Rights Component) / Charter of Solidarity
notes: IndustriALL founded 2012. Represents 50M+ workers in 140+ countries in mining, energy, and manufacturing. Responsible Mining Standard tool supports unions and communities to protect workers' rights. Covers: collective bargaining rights, freedom of association, living wages, maternity leave, health/safety, grievance mechanisms, anti-child labour. Charter of Solidarity addresses corporate violations.

document_title: Safety and Health in Mines Convention C176 (1995) and Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Underground Coal Mines (2006)
profession_name: Mine worker / mine operator / mining company
notes: C176 (1995) is legally binding for ratifying states. Covers: risk notification, mine design, safe operation, emergency procedures, occupational health, worker rights in mines. Supplemented by Code of Practice on Underground Coal Mines (2006) and Code of Practice on Opencast Mines (2018, see below).

document_title: Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Opencast Mines
profession_name: Opencast / surface mine worker and operator
notes: Revised 2018 (original 1991). 11 chapters covering: purpose/objectives, stakeholder duties, safety and health committees, fundamental principles (including risk assessment and OSH management), specific hazards, general controls, work organization. Reflects changes in industry including interaction between large-scale and artisanal mining, and automated machinery. Supplements C176.
